visual.general_description: Radiograph-film style montage of 30 axial contrast CT slices (6 rows by 5 columns) from the upper abdomen to the pelvis showing a very large, low-attenuation, multiloculated abdominal mass occupying most of the abdominal and pelvic cavity.
visual.detailed_description: Each tile is an axial slice on a dark background with overlaid text. The top row shows upper abdominal slices with liver, spleen and the beginning of the mass. In the second to fourth rows a very large, well-defined, heterogeneous low-attenuation mass with thin internal septations occupies most of the abdomen, displaces gas-containing bowel loops toward one side; the vertebra, a bright kidney-like structure and bowel are visible beside it. Lower rows show the mass filling the pelvis, with the pelvic bones in the last rows, where the mass becomes smaller. Burned-in text in every tile includes a patient name, study or accession number, scan date and time, an age and sex abbreviation, window settings and scanner and protocol text. The tiles are partly photographed film with glare and moire. No panel letters or arrows are present.

visual.general_description: Color photograph of a smooth, pink, glossy, ovoid encapsulated mass held in a gloved hand over a green surgical drape beside a tape measure.
visual.detailed_description: An ovoid, lobulated mass with a thin glistening capsule is cradled from below by a gloved hand. Its surface is pale pink to yellowish with a network of fine red vessels and small areas of blood staining and adherent transparent tape or film. A paper or cloth tape measure with printed centimeter numbers runs across the green drape above the mass, partly held by a second gloved hand at the top; the numbers visible run from about 1 to the mid twenties. The mass is not aligned with the tape, so no measurement can be read from the image. Dark fluid staining is visible on the drape at the lower right. No panel letters, labels, text or patient identifiers are visible.
